why: The border IS the shape here, not a boundary around one. A spinner is a ring drawn as a 2px border at 25% of currentColor with one edge (border-t-current) fully opaque, rotated by the motion layer; the arc that reads as progress is the difference between those two edges. There is no fill and no inset shadow that draws a partial ring, and a step in paper tone cannot rotate. RULES.md 2.7 rules on strokes that SEPARATE two things, which this does not.

The same spinner arc, inlined into the button's own busy state rather than imported, so that a busy button never depends on Spinner's own layout. Identical shape, identical reason, and the two are checked together: if one stops drawing its ring the rot check deletes that entry and leaves this one, which is the signal that they have drifted apart.

A drop target, and RULES.md 2.7's own sentence blesses it: form fields and selection controls are the two places a hairline is allowed at all. The dashed edge is also doing work no fill can do — dashed is the one stroke style that reads as PROVISIONAL, which is what an empty drop zone is saying, and the same element restates it in the destructive tone when a file is rejected.

This is not a picture choosing to letterbox; it is the component IMPLEMENTING the `fit` prop, and the two branches of a ternary whose default is `cover`. The client's 2026-09-09 ruling is about what a picture does when nobody says otherwise, and nobody saying otherwise already produces cover here — every call site in this repository and every one in the consuming app takes that default except the two that explicitly ask not to. Deleting the branch would also break RULES.md 9.1 outright: a variant value may never be dropped, because an app pinned to an older tag would stop compiling on the day it upgraded. So the escape hatch stays, and this entry is the record that it was weighed rather than overlooked. It rot-checks against the branch itself: the day `fit` stops offering `contain`, this line goes red and is deleted with it.

Not a colour: `0 0 #0000` is CSS's way of writing a shadow that paints nothing, set on --hairline-strong to switch OFF the note field's ring for the one composer that must not look like a field. `transparent` would be a named colour, which RULES.md 2.2 refuses outright, so the four-digit hex is the least-wrong spelling of nothing available. If tokens.css ever declares a --shadow-none, this line goes with it.

EXCEPTION D, a form control's own edge — and this is the file that defines it. RULES.md 2.7 blesses exactly two places, 'form fields and selection controls', and CH09 states the two strengths: --hair-strong standing, --hair when disabled, plus chapter 9's poppy at 65% for error. Nothing is contained by this stroke; it is what tells a reader the box is typeable at all, and the kit has no fill that says the same thing without also saying 'button'.

EXCEPTION D, a form control's own edge. The same three strengths input.tsx draws, on the 24 box rather than the pill: --hair-strong standing, --hair disabled, the 65% poppy on error. It is the field affordance, not a box around a container.

EXCEPTION D for the standing and disabled strokes, and EXCEPTION C for the two that fire on focus and on open. A select trigger IS a field, so it takes the field hairline; and 'the hairline goes to ink' on focus/open is the artifact's own answer to what an open select looks like. The ink one is a selection affordance in the strict sense - removing it would leave the reader no indication which control the list belongs to - and RULES.md 3.1's global ring is beside it, not instead of it.

EXCEPTION D for the trigger's own two strengths and its 65% poppy error, EXCEPTION C for the ink stroke on data-[open=true], and EXCEPTION E for the ring on data-[today=true]: that last one IS the today marker inside the day grid, a mark rather than a box, and nothing is contained by it. Three exceptions in one file because the file draws a field, a state and a mark, and saying so is cheaper than three near-identical entries.

EXCEPTION D for the field's own --border stroke and EXCEPTION C for the ink one on focus-visible. The control is a field in every respect the kit measures, and its focus stroke is the same 'hairline goes to ink' move select.tsx makes, for the same reason.

EXCEPTION D, a selection control - RULES.md 2.7's second blessed place, named in that sentence. The 22 mark carries --hair-strong unchecked, --hair disabled and chapter 9's 65% poppy on error, including on the checked and indeterminate states, so an invalid box still reads as invalid after it is ticked. The mark has no interior to be a container of.
EXCEPTION D, a selection control. A radio is the checkbox at pill radius and inherits both strengths for the same reason; the comment in that file states the inheritance explicitly.

EXCEPTION D, a form control. A signature pad is a field with a canvas in it: its default, hover, filled and error skins move the hairline's TONE and never its thickness, which is the field grammar chapter 9 sets out. Remove it and the pad becomes an unmarked rectangle of paper that a reader has no reason to touch.

EXCEPTION D, a form control. The drop zone's rejected state draws chapter 9's 65% poppy edge. The zone's own dashed border is a separate exception under the borders law in this same file, for a different reason recorded there; this entry covers the inset one only.

EXCEPTION D, form controls. Three strokes: the facet's selection control at --hair-strong, chapter 9's error edge, and the disabled chip-field's quiet --hair beside its disabled fill and ink. The bar's ordinary chips carry NO stroke - that was removed earlier and its history is written in the file - so what is left here is fields and a selection control only.

EXCEPTION D, a form control, and this one is MEASURED rather than argued. On a phone in the dark palette, 25 Aug 2026, --surface-raised sat one step off the panel, the composer pill vanished, and the reader saw a bare placeholder floating over a dead Send: 'the conversation section is completely broken'. The 20% ring is what says the field is real. The same file's --hairline-start indent is a one-edge separator and is not this law's subject.

EXCEPTION D, a selection control. The NOT-HELD slot is --card behind override 42's stroke; the HELD slot is --surface-inverse and draws none. The stroke is what says 'there is a control here and it is off', which is the same job checkbox.tsx's unchecked mark does, drawn at matrix scale.

EXCEPTION E, a stroke that IS the object. These four are the step MARK for a step not yet reached - a disc on the rail and a pill on the row - drawn on --surface-idle or --surface-lift, whose fill sits under the contrast law's own boundary floor and is DISCHARGED by precisely this ring (check-contrast.mjs names these three lines by number on every run). There is no container under it and no paper step available: the tier below --surface-idle is the page itself.

EXCEPTION E, a stroke that IS the object. The pending step's numbered disc, the row-shaped twin of status-stepper's rail mark, for the identical reason: raised paper with a hairline and a tertiary number is the whole drawing, not a box around one.

EXCEPTION C for the two --hairline-ink strokes and EXCEPTION E for the legend's pending swatch. The ink pair is override 33's selection ring on a chosen node - the kit's own 1px selection treatment, and removing it leaves a reader no way to see which node they picked. The swatch is a colour sample; a pale sample on pale paper has no edge of its own without one.

EXCEPTION E, a stroke that IS the object - and RULES.md 2.7 blesses it by name: variant='outline' is the single UNCOLOURED badge and therefore 'the only badge that draws a hairline'. Section 9.1 forbids dropping a variant value outright, so it could not go even if it were wanted. OPEN QUESTION FOR THE CLIENT, 23 Sep 2026: a chip is arguably a small container, and she has ruled on pill strokes before ('pills no border!'). Standing until she says otherwise.

EXCEPTION E, a stroke that IS the object. A 32px colour SWATCH. The file's own note states the case: a pale swatch on pale paper is invisible without its own edge, and the edge is the sample's boundary rather than a box around anything.

EXCEPTION E for the 14px colour swatch, same reason as brand.tsx's, and EXCEPTION C for the --hairline-ink stroke on a chosen theme tile, which is override 33's selection ring. The three card-and-panel PICTURES in this file wore a hairline until 23 Sep 2026 and do not any more: a picture of a card must wear what a card wears.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE CLIENT, 23 Sep 2026 - provisionally standing. By shape this IS a box around a container and would be removed under 2.8. The file's own header states the counter-argument: an embed paints content this system does not control, and off-beige on off-beige has no edge at all, so taking the stroke off lets a third party's page bleed into ours with nothing to say where one ends. Left drawn rather than guessed at either way; this entry is the record that it was weighed.

OPEN QUESTION FOR THE CLIENT, 23 Sep 2026 - provisionally standing. A stroke on all four edges of a container, which 2.8 removes - except that it is tinted --warning at 35%, so it is carrying a STATUS rather than drawing an outline, and the bar has no second paper tone to fall back to if it goes. The same color-mix shape select.tsx and date-picker.tsx use for a tinted field edge. Left drawn; this entry is the record that it was weighed.
